text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHall(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
NeedsMoneyForTuition(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah ::: Hannah.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoneyForTuition(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school work in student jobs on campus, then they need to earn money to help pay for their college tuition.
∀x (OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school order takeout frequently in college, then they work in student jobs on campus.
∀x (OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHall(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People at Mary's school order takeout frequently or enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy the dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x)) ::: If people enjoy the dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of time eating and catching up in the dining halls.
Hannah ∧ AtSchool(Hannah) ∧ WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and works in student jobs.
(NeedsMoneyForTuition(Hannah) → (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ NeedsMoneyForTuition(Hannah))) ::: If Hannah needs to earn money, then she is not a picky eater and needs to earn money.

Conclusion:
NeedsMoneyForTuition(Hannah) ::: Hannah needs to earn money to help pay for her college tuition.
